gaps.sentence: She ___ have received your email — her inbox was full last week.
gaps.hint: ruled out as a past possibility
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' plus the participle rules out a past possibility: can't have received.

gaps.sentence: I ___ rather stay at home tonight, if that is all right.
gaps.explanation: 'Would rather' expresses preference: would rather stay.

gaps.sentence: It is Saturday tomorrow, so I ___ get up early.
gaps.hint: an absence of obligation at weekends
gaps.explanation: 'Don't have to' shows there is no obligation: don't have to get up.

gaps.sentence: You ___ to be more careful with your passwords.
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' behaves like 'should' and always takes 'to': ought to be.

gaps.sentence: We ___ to be at the airport three hours before long-haul flights.
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' shows obligation from outside the speaker: have to be.

gaps.sentence: I ___ help thinking he is hiding something.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't help' plus -ing means being unable to stop a feeling: can't help thinking.

gaps.sentence: Visitors ___ to leave the gallery by 6 p.m.
gaps.hint: have to takes the full infinitive
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' takes the full infinitive with 'to': have to leave.

gaps.sentence: The medicine ___ be kept out of the reach of children.
gaps.explanation: Written instructions use 'must' for essential requirements: must be kept.
